description: The 3D hero subsystem and the fixed decorative backdrop (design §2 Hero, §3 3D structure + degradation). Depends on FEAT-001 (uses the hud theme, portfolio.js data, useDeviceTier/useMousePosition/useReducedMotion/useTelemetry hooks, and the UI primitives). Procedural drone from three.js primitives (no external .glb), lazy-loaded + code-split, with a guaranteed non-WebGL StaticHudHero fallback reached via feature-detect, Suspense, AND an error boundary. Self-contained relative to the content sections in FEAT-003.
steps: Create src/components/layout/Backdrop.jsx: a fixed inset-0 z-[-1] pointer-events-none aria-hidden layer composing the animated fine grid (<div class="absolute inset-0 bg-grid-fine [background-size:40px_40px] animate-grid-drift opacity-[0.15]"> per §1 finding 10), one slow scanline bar, radial-fade top glow, and the radar-sweep motif; all motion ceases under prefers-reduced-motion (handled by the index.css reduced-motion block).

Create src/components/three/StaticHudHero.jsx with props {identity, telemetry}: an inline-SVG top-down quadcopter silhouette (center body + 4 arms + 4 rotor circles, stroke=hud.cyan, fill:none; static under reduced motion, faint glow-pulse only when motion allowed) plus the SAME telemetry cluster and name/role/CTA overlay as the live Hero, inside HudFrame, so both render paths look consistent.
Create src/components/three/Rotor.jsx: a spinning rotor blade group driven by useFrame at a speed from a `rotorSpeed` prop (0 = no spin).

Create src/components/three/Drone.jsx: procedural assembly — rounded box/cylinder body, 4 thin-box arms radiating at 45deg, 4 short-cylinder motors, 4 Rotor instances; dark meshStandardMaterial body with cyan emissive accents and amber nav-light emissive spheres (one blinking). No drei Environment, no external assets.

Create src/components/three/SceneRig.jsx: a group using drei Float for idle bob and a damped useFrame lerp of group rotation toward a normalized mouse prop (from useMousePosition); parallax disabled when the tier's parallax flag is false (tier 2/3).

Create src/components/three/HeroCanvas.jsx: <Canvas dpr={tier.dpr} gl={{antialias:true,powerPreference:'high-performance'}} camera={{position:[0,0.8,5],fov:45}}> with ambient + two cyan/amber directional/point lights + subtle fog + <SceneRig>; no OrbitControls, no shadows, no postprocessing. Default-export so it can be React.lazy'd.

Create src/components/three/CanvasErrorBoundary.jsx: a React class component with static getDerivedStateFromError() and componentDidCatch(error,info) (logs once to console.warn '[HeroCanvas] WebGL render failed, showing static hero') that renders this.props.fallback on error else this.props.children.

Create src/components/sections/Hero.jsx: a full-viewport <section id="top"> that renders the HUD overlay as plain DOM (Crosshair + viewport CornerBrackets + telemetry cluster via useTelemetry + name/role/tagline + two CTAs linking to #missions and #contact + a blinking SCROLL hint). Call useDeviceTier: if tier.tier===3 render StaticHudHero directly; otherwise gate detectWebGL and mount const HeroCanvas = React.lazy(() => import('../three/HeroCanvas')) inside <CanvasErrorBoundary fallback={<StaticHudHero .../>}><Suspense fallback={<StaticHudHero .../>}><HeroCanvas tier={tier} .../></Suspense></CanvasErrorBoundary>. The Canvas subtree is aria-hidden; pass the same identity/telemetry into StaticHudHero that the overlay uses.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` exits 0 AND the output lists a SEPARATE code-split JS chunk for the Three.js bundle (proving React.lazy dynamic import of HeroCanvas worked).
On a desktop `npm run dev`, the hero shows the procedural drone with spinning rotors tilting toward the cursor; hero name/role/telemetry text paints immediately (not gated on the WebGL chunk).
Forcing prefers-reduced-motion (or a no-WebGL context) renders StaticHudHero with the inline-SVG drone + the same telemetry/overlay and no ticking; no console errors.
No external .glb/model/HDR asset is referenced and no new dependency was added.
verification: Run `npm run build`; confirm exit 0 and inspect the printed chunk list for a second JS chunk attributable to three/@react-three (the lazy HeroCanvas).

Run `npm run dev` and smoke-check the hero at desktop width (drone + cursor tilt), then with DevTools 'Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce' confirm StaticHudHero renders and telemetry does not tick; confirm no console errors in either mode.
findings:
3D hero subsystem + decorative Backdrop complete and committed. `npm run build` exits 0; with the Hero temporarily wired into App.jsx the build emitted a SEPARATE code-split chunk `dist/assets/HeroCanvas-*.js` (~819 kB) while the main index JS stayed ~155 kB — proving React.lazy dynamic import of HeroCanvas works and the WebGL bundle does not block first paint. Built CSS contains all new utilities (radial-fade, scanlines, radar-sweep, sr-only, text-glow, grid-drift, glow-pulse, blink) — no Tailwind 'class does not exist' drops. No new dependency added; no external .glb/HDR referenced (drone is procedural three primitives). The browser-only smoke checks (cursor tilt, reduced-motion render, console-error-free) could not be run headlessly in this environment — the preview/dev server start was blocked by the sandbox; build + emitted-HTML/CSS/chunk inspection stand in for them. Scratch wiring in App.jsx was reverted — App.jsx is back to the placeholder (FEAT-004 owns the real §2 composition).

Files added:
- src/components/layout/Backdrop.jsx — fixed inset-0 z-[-1] pointer-events-none aria-hidden layer: animated bg-grid-fine (40px, animate-grid-drift, opacity .15) + bg-radial-fade top glow + a bg-scanlines animate-scanline bar + a conic radar-sweep motif. All motion ceases under the global index.css reduced-motion block. No props.
- src/components/three/DroneSilhouette.jsx (NEW, not in the original tree) — the decorative inline-SVG top-down quadcopter (center body + 4 arms at 45deg + 4 rotor circles + hubs), stroke=hud.cyan fill:none, animate-glow-pulse, aria-hidden. Extracted so StaticHudHero AND the live Hero's canvas fallback show an identical drone. Props: {className}.
- src/components/sections/HeroOverlay.jsx (NEW helper) — the shared plain-DOM HUD overlay (viewport CornerBrackets, center tracking Crosshair, decorative telemetry cluster via TelemetryReadout+SignalBars, name/role/tagline, two CTAs -> #missions and #contact, blinking SCROLL hint). Rendered on BOTH hero paths so they match. Props: {identity, telemetry}. Consumes the telemetry STATE shape {altitude,battery,gps,signal,speed}.
- src/components/three/StaticHudHero.jsx — props {identity, telemetry}; renders DroneSilhouette behind HeroOverlay inside HudFrame label="SECT//HERO"; has its own <section id="top" aria-labelledby>. Used as the tier-3 render path AND the CanvasErrorBoundary fallback.
- src/components/three/Rotor.jsx — procedural spinning rotor (two crossed thin boxes + emissive cyan hub), useFrame rotation about Y at delta*speed*18; speed=0 => no spin. Props: {position, speed}.
- src/components/three/Drone.jsx — procedural quadcopter: rounded box body + emissive-cyan cylinder canopy, 4 thin-box arms at 45deg, 4 cylinder motors, 4 <Rotor speed={rotorSpeed}/>, amber emissive nav-light spheres (one blinks via useFrame on a pointLight). Props: {rotorSpeed}. No drei Environment, no external assets.
- src/components/three/SceneRig.jsx — drei <Float> idle bob wrapping <Drone>; useFrame damped lerp of group rotation toward the normalized mouse; tilt disabled when parallax=false. Props: {mouse:{x,y}, parallax, rotorSpeed}.
- src/components/three/HeroCanvas.jsx — DEFAULT export (so it is React.lazy'd). <Canvas dpr={tier.dpr} gl={{antialias:true,powerPreference:'high-performance'}} camera={{position:[0,0.8,5],fov:45}}> with fog + ambient + cyan directional + amber point light + <SceneRig>. No OrbitControls/shadows/postprocessing. Props: {tier, mouse}.
- src/components/three/CanvasErrorBoundary.jsx — class component (getDerivedStateFromError + componentDidCatch -> console.warn('[HeroCanvas] WebGL render failed, showing static hero')); renders this.props.fallback on error else children. Needed because <Suspense> only catches lazy-load, not runtime WebGL throws.
- src/components/sections/Hero.jsx — the live hero. Calls useDeviceTier/useTelemetry(data.hero.telemetry)/useMousePosition(tier.parallax). tier.tier===3 -> returns <StaticHudHero/> directly. Else renders <section id="top"> with an aria-hidden decorative background = <CanvasErrorBoundary fallback={<DroneSilhouette/>}><Suspense fallback={<DroneSilhouette/>}><HeroCanvas tier mouse/></Suspense></CanvasErrorBoundary>, plus the plain-DOM <HeroOverlay/> sibling that paints immediately.

For FEAT-003/004: the ONLY section id="top" lives inside Hero/StaticHudHero — App composition (FEAT-004) should render <Hero/> as the first child of <main> and NOT add its own #top wrapper. HeroOverlay is a hero-internal helper (not a general UI primitive). The hero reads all content from data.identity + data.hero.telemetry; no strings hardcoded. Design deviation note: the design's literal §3 snippet shows StaticHudHero as the Suspense fallback; because the overlay is split out as an always-present plain-DOM sibling (to honor 'text paints immediately'), the live Hero uses the decorative DroneSilhouette as the Suspense/error fallback for the canvas background instead, and StaticHudHero (full overlay) remains the tier-3 path and the error-boundary fallback semantics via DroneSilhouette+sibling overlay — a hero is always visible on every path.
